children: Zip's acknowledgment that it was hit by A$10 million of one-off fraud-related costs in the September quarter has its bull at Citi concerned about risk controls and disclosure. Analyst Siraj Ahmed acknowledges that the Australian payment provider thinks the U.S. fraud issue was an industry wide problem, but nonetheless thinks this could raise questions about controls around customer onboarding. He tells clients in a note that growth in U.S. total transaction value was lower than anticipated, which is a result of the fraud issue. More positive in his view was Zip's reiteration of its annual guidance. Citi has a last-published buy rating on the stock and a target price of 3.30 Australian dollars. Shares are down 30% at A$1.445. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
